title: Implementation and Evaluation of a Machine Learned Mesoscale Eddy Parameterization Into a Numerical Ocean Circulation Model
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: subgrid mesoscale eddy momentum forcing (mean and standard deviation of Gaussian distribution)
code_availability: The source code of the MOM6 version used for implementing the ML parameterization is accessible through Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7663075), while the CNN model files used for the online evaluation in this study (GZ21) can also be accessed via Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7663062). Setup files for the wind-driven double gyre case are available at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7663128).
testbed_rationale: Provides a clean, standardized, and open multi-resolution (1/4° to 1/32°) MOM6 double-gyre benchmark configuration on Zenodo with complete setup files and pretrained CNN weights, explicitly designed for testing subgrid ocean eddy parameterizations online.
pain_points: Language interoperability: bridging compiled Fortran (MOM6) and Python (PyTorch) required using Forpy, with manual array conversion between Fortran and NumPy.
Stencil and halo width: The CNN's 21x21 stencil required expanding parallel MPI halo widths to 10 (vs. MOM6's default 3-4), increasing memory and communication complexity.
Prohibitive CPU inference costs: Inference on CPUs took ~10x more processing time than the MOM6 dynamical core (~268,000 FLOPs per grid point).

Hardware and parallelization constraints: GPU inference reduced costs significantly via CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS), but MPS limits of 16 CPU cores per GPU required custom data-gathering MPI interfaces.
Grid staggering mismatch: MOM6 uses an Arakawa C-grid while the CNN was trained on co-located B-grid velocities, necessitating spatial interpolation to and from velocity points.
Lateral boundary artifacts: The CNN produced spurious, strongly sheared eddy structures near rigid walls and bathymetry because training data excluded land/coastal regions.
Vertical generalization: A model trained solely on surface data over-energized upper layers while under-energizing lower layers, requiring empirical layer-by-layer tuning coefficients.
extraction_notes: The paper implements and tests the pre-existing stochastic CNN parameterization from Guillaumin and Zanna (2021; GZ21) within MOM6 using Forpy to evaluate online stability, generalization to different flow regimes/vertical layers, and computational overhead on CPUs vs. GPUs.
